extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the GAP computer algebra system (people writing GAP code that manipulates lists, ranges, and sets)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation of GAP operations for lists, sorted lists, sets, ranges, and related utilities, describing semantics, preconditions, and behavior (including mutable vs immutable and stable vs unstable behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: ConstantTimeAccessList behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: If list is already a constant time access list, ConstantTimeAccessList returns an immutable copy of list directly. Otherwise it puts all elements and holes of list into a new list and makes that list immutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to obtain an immutable constant-time-access representation; converts non-constant-time lists by copying elements and holes into a new list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sorting algorithm families
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP implements three different families of sorting algorithms: pattern-defeating quicksort (default), stable functions (begin Stable) using merge sort, and Shell using shell sort (the previous default). Sortex and SortingPerm are also stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default algorithm is pattern-defeating quicksort for performance on partially sorted lists and good worst-case behaviour; choose Stable* functions when stability is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sort(list[, func]) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort sorts the list list in increasing order. One-argument form uses operator <; two-argument form uses func which must take two arguments and return true if the first is strictly smaller than the second.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If list is heterogeneous, user must ensure < is defined for all element pairs. Sort changes the list in place and returns nothing; use ShallowCopy to keep the original and Reversed to get decreasing order.

rubrics_metrics.name: StableSort behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: StableSort behaves identically to Sort except it keeps elements which compare equal in the same relative order, while Sort may change their relative order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use StableSort when the relative order of equal elements must be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: SortBy(list, func) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: SortBy sorts the list into an order such that func(list[i]) <= func(list[i+1]) for all i. func must be a unary function returning comparable values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each func(list[i]) is computed once and stored, making SortBy more efficient than a two-argument Sort in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: StableSortBy behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: StableSortBy behaves the same as SortBy except that it preserves the relative order of elements that compare equal under func.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when sort-key stability is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: SortParallel(list1, list2[, func]) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: SortParallel sorts list1 like Sort and applies the same exchanges to list2, which must have at least as many elements as list1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to keep a secondary list in sync with reordering of a primary list. If multiple stable outcomes exist, SortParallel may produce different valid results; StableSortParallel guarantees preservation of equal-element order in list1.

rubrics_metrics.name: StableSortParallel behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: StableSortParallel behaves identically to SortParallel but keeps elements in list1 that compare equal in the same relative order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer StableSortParallel when determinism with equal keys is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sortex(list[, func]) behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: Sortex sorts the list and returns a permutation that can be applied to list to obtain the sorted list. The returned permutation keeps elements which compare equal in the same relative order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Sortex to compute a permutation instead of reordering the list in place; Permuted can apply the permutation to other lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: SortingPerm(list) behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: SortingPerm returns the same permutation as Sortex but does not change the argument list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you need the sorting permutation without modifying the original list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strictly sorted lists and IsSSortedList
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP exploits sortedness automatically only if the list is strictly sorted, indicated by the property IsSSortedList.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists with mutable entries cannot store that they are strictly sorted and must be rechecked when asked; using sorted lists with mutable elements may slow computations because checks are performed when functions expecting sorted input are called.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper set representation (strictly sorted lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper set in GAP is represented by a strictly sorted list without holes and duplicates; this representation is guaranteed and may be relied upon in functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since proper sets are represented this way, algorithms can assume sortedness/no-holes/no-duplicates for set-specific operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiset representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A multiset is represented by a sorted list without holes that may have duplicates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sorted lists without holes to represent multisets where multiplicity matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership test \in for strictly sorted lists
rubrics_metrics.description: For a list that stores it is strictly sorted, the membership test obj in list uses binary search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use strictly sorted lists to get efficient membership tests via binary search.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsEqualSet(list1, list2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether list1 and list2 are equal when viewed as sets: every element of list1 is an element of list2 and vice versa. If an argument is not a proper set, Set is applied first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both lists are proper sets, this is equivalent to equality as lists but more efficient; use IsEqualSet rather than converting to Set explicitly when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsSubsetSet(list1, list2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether every element of list2 is contained in list1. If an argument is not a proper set, Set is applied first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preconditions: set arguments are converted via Set when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: AddSet(set, obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds obj to the proper set set. If obj is already contained it is not changed; otherwise obj is inserted at the correct position so set remains a proper set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: obj must be in the same family as each element of set.

rubrics_metrics.name: RemoveSet(set, obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes obj from the proper set set. If obj is not contained nothing changes; if removed, following elements are moved one position forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operation mutates the set (list) in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: UniteSet(set, list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unites the proper set set with list; equivalent to adding all elements of list to set (see AddSet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If list is not a proper set it is silently first converted with Set.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntersectSet(set, list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Intersects the proper set set with list; equivalent to removing from set all elements that are not contained in list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutates set and returns the resulting proper set; second argument may be converted via Set if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: SubtractSet(set, list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtracts list from the proper set set; equivalent to removing from set all elements of list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutates set in place; list converted via Set if not a proper set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concatenation(list1, list2, ...)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the concatenation of lists list1, list2, etc.; holes are preserved at corresponding positions. In the single-argument form, the argument must be a dense list of lists to concatenate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is a new mutable list (not identical to any input) but its elements are identical to corresponding elements of inputs. Concatenation leaves arguments unchanged (contrasts with Append).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compacted(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a new mutable list containing the elements of list in the same order but omitting the holes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to create a dense copy of a list with holes removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collected(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a new list new that contains for each element elm of list a pair [elm, count] where count is the number of occurrences; the order corresponds to ordering of elm, so result is sorted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires that comparison via < is defined for all pairs of elements in list.

rubrics_metrics.name: DuplicateFreeList(list) / Unique(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a new mutable list whose entries are the elements of list with duplicates removed. DuplicateFreeList uses only = comparison and will not sort the result. Unique is a synonym.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used when elements are not in the same family. If elements can be compared with <, Set is much more efficient (but requires comparability).

rubrics_metrics.name: AsDuplicateFreeList(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the same result as DuplicateFreeList but the result is immutable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when an immutable duplicate-free list is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the list of all elements contained in list or its sublists recursively (flattening).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recurses into sublists, concatenating their Flat results; useful to linearize nested list structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reversed(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a new mutable list containing elements of a dense list in reversed order. The argument is unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Result is a new list whose elements are identical to corresponding elements of argument. Developers adapting this for custom list types must install methods for ReversedOp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shuffle(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Permutes the entries of list randomly in place and returns list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument must be a dense mutable list. Use Reset(GlobalMersenneTwister, seed) for reproducible shuffles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply(list, func)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies func to every element of a dense mutable list and replaces each element by the corresponding return value (destructive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply changes its argument; the nondestructive counterpart is List.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform(list, func)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies func to every element of list, discarding any return values. Does not return a value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to run side-effecting operations over list elements (e.g., printing).

rubrics_metrics.name: PermListList(list1, list2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a permutation p of [1..Length(list1)] such that list1[i^p] = list2[i]. Returns fail if no such permutation exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to compute a permutation mapping one list to another when such a permutation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum(obj1, obj2, ...) and Maximum(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: In first form returns one argument that is ≥ all others. In second form takes a homogeneous list and returns its maximum. Lists are compared elementwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons must be defined (usually elements must be in same family). To get index of maximum use PositionMaximum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum(obj1, obj2, ...) and Minimum(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogous to Maximum: returns a minimum argument or the minimum element of a homogeneous list; lists compared elementwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons must be defined; use PositionMinimum for index.

rubrics_metrics.name: MaximumList(list[, seed]) and MinimumList(list[, seed])
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the maximum or minimum of the elements in list. If seed is supplied the result is the max/min of union of list and seed to allow application to empty lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These operations are invoked by Maximum/Minimum and can have special methods for certain list types (e.g., ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartesian(list1, list2, ...)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the cartesian product as a list of tuples (lists) where the last index runs fastest. Total number of tuples is the product of lengths; cart is empty iff any argument is empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cartesian contains duplicates iff some argument contains duplicates. The cart is a proper set iff all argument lists are proper sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: IteratorOfCartesianProduct(list1, list2, ...)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns an iterator over the cartesian product of the argument lists, yielding tuples in lexicographic order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended for large cartesian products to avoid memory/time costs of generating the full product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permuted(list, perm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a new list whose elements are the elements of list permuted according to permutation perm: new[i^perm] = list[i] whenever list[i] is bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with permutations computed by Sortex/SortingPerm to reorder copies of lists without modifying originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: List(list[, func])
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a new mutable list new of the same length as list; new[i] is unbound if list[i] is unbound, otherwise new[i] = func(list[i]). Default func is IdFunc so List(list) equals ShallowCopy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves holes/unbound entries; developers adapting for custom list types must install ListOp methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered(listorcoll, func)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a new list containing elements of the list or collection for which func returns true. If the first argument is a list, order is preserved; holes are ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every element must make func return either true or false or an error is signalled. Result elements are identical to argument elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number(listorcoll[, func])
rubrics_metrics.description: Called with a list, returns the number of bound entries. With func, returns count of elements for which func returns true; for dense lists Number, Length, and Size coincide but with holes Number counts bound entries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: func must return true/false for each element; use Filtered to extract the elements themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: First(list[, func])
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the first element of list for which func returns true; if func omitted returns the first element. list may contain holes. If none satisfy, returns fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: func must return true/false for every element or an error is signalled. Use PositionProperty to find the position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Last(list[, func])
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the last element of list for which func returns true; analogous to First but for the last element; returns fail if none match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: list may contain holes; developers can install LastOp for custom list types.

rubrics_metrics.name: ForAll(listorcoll, func)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether func returns true for all elements in list or collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for universal property checks over collections; developers can install ForAllOp for custom types.

rubrics_metrics.name: ForAny(listorcoll, func)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether func returns true for at least one element in list or collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for existential checks; developers can install ForAnyOp for custom types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product(listorcoll[, func][, init])
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns product of elements, or product of func applied to elements. Returns 1 for empty first argument. If init supplied returns product of init and elements (useful when empty and different identity desired).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arithmetic rules apply: result immutable iff all factors are immutable. Single-element results return the element itself (no shallow copy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum(listorcoll[, func][, init])
rubrics_metrics.description: Analogous to Product: returns sum of elements or sum of func applied to elements; returns 0 for empty; with init uses init as additive identity if desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arithmetic rules apply; single-element behavior similar to Product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterated(list, f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns f(...f(f(list[1],list[2]),list[3])...,list[n]) — iterated application of binary function f over list elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for cumulative reductions (e.g., Gcd over a list).

rubrics_metrics.name: ListN(list1, list2, ..., listn, f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies the n-argument function f elementwise to the argument lists; the i-th entry of the result is f(list1[i], list2[i], ..., listn[i]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists should be aligned by index; result is a new list of computed values.

rubrics_metrics.name: ListX(arg1, arg2, ..., argn, func)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalized list construction: each argument may be a list/collection (introduces a loop), a function returning a list/collection (nested loop dependant on outer variables), or a predicate (introduces an if). The last argument func is applied to loop variables and results are collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ListX can express nested loops and filters compactly; examples show equivalence to nested for/if/od constructs and how to compute pairs or strictly sorted pairs via ListX with <.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetX(arg1, arg2, ..., func)
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as ListX except the result list of SetX is strictly sorted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SetX when the resulting collection should be a proper set (sorted, no holes, no duplicates).

rubrics_metrics.name: SumX(arg1, arg2, ..., func) and ProductX(arg1, arg2, ..., func)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the sum or product of the elements in the list obtained by calling ListX with the same arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience operations combining ListX generation with aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range definition and syntactic constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: A range is a dense list of integers in arithmetic progression; syntactic forms are [first, second..last] or [first..last] (increment 1). If first>last then [first..last] is empty by definition. last-first must be divisible by increment (second-first) or an error is signalled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: first, second, last and length must be small integers (chapter 14). Ranges are lists and support indexing, membership tests, and assignment (assignment may convert a compact representation into a plain list).

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRange(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests if obj is a range (a dense list of integers that is also a range as per definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns true for empty list and singletons that satisfy range properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsRangeRep(obj)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests whether obj is represented internally as a range (IsRangeRep) — i.e., stored compactly by first value, increment, and last value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A list may be mathematically a range but not be represented as IsRangeRep; lists created by the syntactic construct [first..last] are IsRangeRep. Modifying such objects may convert them to plain lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: ConvertToRangeRep(list)
rubrics_metrics.description: If list is a range, ConvertToRangeRep changes its representation to the compact IsRangeRep representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to convert a plain list that is mathematically a range into the internal compact range representation.
